scope: Unexecuted PI hypothesis for integration with corrected CAD; requires one common final profile and all native acceptance tests

derivation.proportional_selection: Observed resisting torque about4.4Nm divided by an estimated residual speed-error target0.15rad/s requiresP>=29.33Nms/rad; chooseP30. The error target is a controller-design hypothesis, not a relaxed physical acceptance tolerance.
derivation.steady_error_example: At4.4Nm load, P12 with integral saturated at1Nm requires about(4.4-1)/12=.2833rad/s error, matching the observed shortfall. P30 gives.1133rad/s under that same integral contribution; allowing the integral to supply the actual load removes this artificial1Nm steady-state ceiling.
derivation.integral_bound_selection: ceil(5.127520532755967/0.5)*0.5=5.5Nm covers the inferred maximum residual traction torque, below the unchanged total6.5Nm motor-command clamp. Keep I4 and D0.
derivation.discrete_analysis: Use each native CAD wheel inertia about its actual Y joint axis, including the parallel-axis COM term. Check h*P/J and the2x2 Euler PI eigenvalues for both integral-update orderings at h=.0001s. This local unsaturated free-wheel check is necessary but does not validate coupled contact dynamics.
derivation.gain_selection: Change only existing wheel_velocity_p_gain from12 to30 and wheel_integral_effort_limit_nm from1 to5.5. Keep I4, D0, total torque6.5Nm, geometry, mass, inertia, friction, masks and all physical acceptance thresholds. Do not claim native PASS before the corrected-CAD full protocol is run.
derivation.hardware_caveat: All gains and6.5Nm capacity remain estimated simulation parameters. No motor torque-speed, current, gearbox or thermal hardware measurement validates them.
